contentHtml:
CUBA—The World Health Organization (WHO) has committed US$2 million to support Cuba’s national immunisation programme and strengthen healthcare delivery during Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus’s visit to the country on November 22, 2026.

Tedros travelled to Cuba at the invitation of Minister of Public Health Dr. José Ángel Portal Miranda.

During the visit, he met President Miguel Díaz-Canel Bermúdez, toured healthcare facilities and held discussions with senior government officials and representatives of WHO and the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO).

The funding will prioritise vaccination services for children and adults, alongside rabies prevention and control.

Cuba has maintained vaccination coverage above 98% for several years, but the rate fell to 95% in 2025, highlighting the need to reinforce immunisation services.

According to WHO, the contribution will support vaccination activities targeting approximately 62,000 newborns, more than 780,000 children and over 110,000 people in other risk groups.

“Cuba’s hard-won public health achievements must be protected,” Tedros said, reaffirming WHO and PAHO’s commitment to maintaining access to essential vaccines and healthcare services.

WHO and PAHO expand healthcare support

The latest commitment forms part of broader international efforts to sustain Cuba’s healthcare system.

Between 2025 and 2026, WHO and PAHO mobilised more than US$14 million through 14 projects targeting healthcare quality, service sustainability and health workforce development.

During his visit, Tedros also toured William Soler University Pediatric Hospital and its paediatric cardiology centre, where he met healthcare workers and families of children receiving treatment.

The delegation delivered medical supplies and equipment mobilised through the PAHO/WHO Emergency team.

The consignment included basic medical care kits, electronic blood pressure monitors, ophthalmoscopes, otoscopes, pulse oximeters, sphygmomanometers, stethoscopes and thermometers.

These supplies are intended to strengthen diagnostic and patient-monitoring capacity at the hospital, supporting the delivery of paediatric and specialist care.

Tedros also met the United Nations Country Team and other development partners to discuss sustained financial and strategic support for Cuba’s public health sector.

Discussions focused on improving coordination and identifying opportunities to align international assistance with the country’s healthcare priorities.

Engagement with Cuba’s biotechnology industry

Beyond healthcare delivery, Tedros met executives from leading Cuban biotechnology companies to discuss developments and challenges facing the country’s pharmaceutical industry.

The discussions covered research and product development in infectious disease prevention and control, Alzheimer’s disease, cancer and diabetes.

The engagement comes as Cuba seeks to maintain its domestic biomedical research and manufacturing capabilities while addressing challenges affecting its healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors.

WHO and PAHO’s engagement with the industry provides an opportunity to strengthen cooperation in vaccine development, medical innovation and access to essential health technologies.

This was Tedros’s second official visit to Cuba as WHO Director-General, following his previous trip in 2018.

He was accompanied by WHO Assistant Director-General for Business Operations Raúl Thomas and Dr Ciro Ugarte, Director of PAHO’s Health Emergencies Department.

Tedros is scheduled to visit other countries in the region during the week.
